title: Elon Musk on DOGE, first-principles execution, and starting SpaceX from a failed Mars plan
summary: In a White House interview with Ted Cruz, Musk explains how he finds waste by going straight to the underlying computer systems, why he insourced manufacturing, and how SpaceX began after failed attempts to buy Russian ICBMs. He also covers his view on patents, work habits and AI timelines.

principles.text: Go to the underlying data systems instead of asking layers of people; that's how you see what is really happening.
principles.quote: the only way to reconcile the databases and get rid of waste and fraud is to um to actually look at the computers and see what's going on

principles.text: Insource when you can't outsource well; do the hard thing yourself and you become the expert.
principles.quote: it's just that I was unable to Outsource it effectively so uh you know the idea in the beginning of Tesla was that we would Outsource almost all the manufacturing

principles.text: Ideas are cheap; execution is the hard part, so don't hoard IP.
principles.quote: the ideas are easy you want ideas to flow maximum to people to get there faster and do things bigger the idea is the easy part uh the hard execution is the hard part

principles.text: File patents only defensively to block patent trolls, then open source them.
principles.quote: we only do patents at Tesla to to avoid patent trolls causing causing trouble so we'll try to look ahead say Okay patent trolls going to Tri P file patents to block certain things will file patents and then open source patent make it free

principles.text: Question the premise: he found the real problem was affordable access to space, not public will, so he built his own rockets.
principles.quote: I actually realized in the in the course of this that my original premise was wrong that that America actually has plenty of will to go to Mars but needs that it just needs a way to go to Mars um that is Affordable

principles.text: Need a philosophical foundation to stay highly motivated through hard, risky ventures.
principles.quote: you have to start with a some sort of philosophical premise in order to have in order for the in order to be in order to be highly motivated you have to have some um philosophical Foundation
